questions.prompt:
When Casey gets frightened suddenly by the dog barking, which nervous system is activated?
Source context: casey is walking down the street when a dog behind a fence barks loudly and casey jumps from fright.
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch211","id":"e499-image1"}]}]

The nervous system activated affects the body in numerous ways. Select the most likely symptoms that Casey will experience.
Source context: casey is walking down the street when a dog behind a fence barks loudly and casey jumps from fright.
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch211","id":"e499-image1"}]}]
options: Dilated pupils, inhibited digestion, contracted bladder.
Relaxed bladder, inhibited digestion, dilated pupils.
Stimulated digestion, constricted pupils, accelerated heart rate.
Slowed heart rate, contracted bladder, dilated pupils.
questions.explanation: B:relaxed bladder,inhibited digestion and dilated pupils.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct definition for ‘target cells.’
options: The cells that hormones act on.
The cells that enzymes act on.
questions.explanation: A:cells with receptors that respond to the hormone.

questions.prompt: Select the incorrect statement below.
options: Nerve impulses can only travel in one direction.
Nerve impulses are electrical messages carried by a nerve cell.
The nervous system is made up of hundreds of nerve cells.
Electrical messages are also known as nerve impulses.
questions.explanation: C:the nervous system contains far more than hundreds of nerve cells. One-way transmission is the normal functional circuit model,not an absolute property of every experimentally stimulated axon.

questions.prompt: A receptor is a specialised nerve. The main function of the receptors is:
options: Send messages from the brain to the muscles
Send messages to the central nervous system from an organ
questions.explanation: D:detect a stimulus;some sensory receptor cells are specialised non-neuronal cells.

questions.prompt: The hypothalamus regulates:
questions.explanation: D:all are regulated directly or indirectly through hypothalamic homeostatic/autonomic control.

questions.prompt: Describe the relationship between the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland.
options: The pituitary is called the “master gland”. The hypothalamus responds to messages    from the pituitary gland.
The hypothalamus secretes hormones that act on the pituitary gland which is also known as the “master gland”.
The hypothalamus is part of the brain and the pituitary gland is located in front of the trachea in the neck.
The hypothalamus constantly checks the conditions within the organs and systems of the body. The pituitary gland checks the activity of the brain.

questions.prompt: During gas exchange in the alveoli of the lungs, ________ moves from the capillaries into the alveoli and _________ moves from the alveoli into the capillaries.
questions.explanation: A:carbon dioxide to alveoli;oxygen to capillaries.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct definition of “homeostasis”
options: The maintenance of a constant internal environment
The ability to react to changes in the internal environment
The releasing of hormones that react to certain stimuli
A pair of hormones that work together and react in opposite ways
questions.explanation: A:maintenance of a relatively stable internal environment within regulated ranges,not perfect constancy.
